title: Leaderboard competition — ranking skill, not variance
description: Design for the rewarded internal competition the brief asks for. The central design choice is that the leaderboard ranks a luck-adjusted statistic computed from a sealed, walk-forward bet log — not profit, not ROI, not this month's hot hand — and that rewards are conditional on gate passage. engine/leaderboard.py implements exactly the scoring written here, and its unit tests are hand-checkable.

sections.title: A. Divisions
sections.description: Separated because a single table would rank a 400-bet totals strategy against a 40-bet prop combo and call the difference skill.

columns.label: Why it is its own table

rows.scope: Pre-game spread only, one club view per game
rows.why_split: Highest liquidity, lowest hold assumption, the only market where a real edge is measurable at human sample sizes.
The primary output of a totals-first architecture; the published mispricing evidence clusters here.
Different price structure (no push), and the published favourite-longshot evidence applies to this family, not to spreads.
Thin limits and high dependence on the availability model; a good week here is often one QB-regime call.
Highest model risk because settlement definitions vary; every entry must name its settlement source (Q-03).

rows.scope: Same-game player prop combinations priced by the joint model
rows.why_split: This is where correlation is either the whole edge or the whole error; it is scored with the dependence correction shown next to the naive product for every bet.

rows.scope: Uncorrelated legs only, per house rule
rows.why_split: Structurally a different product (Nevada requires parlay cards to be reported separately); the hurdle compounds per leg, so the sample requirement is the highest.

rows.scope: Any permitted market where the thesis is an injury/depth event
rows.why_split: Isolating the brief's injury requirement lets us see whether the availability model adds value anywhere, instead of burying it inside a general totals model.
Latency, in-play data and video rights sit behind the exclusive distributor and live hold is widest; excluded by recommendation (Q-20, R-39), pending owner decision.
Not a competition category; the league prohibits these wager classes and our gate refuses them before scoring.

sections.title: B. Scoring — the Luck-Adjusted Score (LAS)
sections.description: One scalar, computable from a bet log with no judgement calls, printed next to its inputs so a reader can disagree with the weights but not with the arithmetic.
columns: why it is in the score

rows.definition: Mean per-dollar expected value versus the closing price (CLV-based), not versus realised PnL.
rows.why: Realised PnL is where luck lives; the closing line is the only unbiased, high-frequency answer to 'was this price good'. Blocked by GAP-01, which is why the competition starts in paper mode.

rows.definition: Rank on the 5th-percentile bootstrap bound of EV_hat, i.e. the pessimistic end of the estimate.
rows.why: This is the anti-luck core of the design: an entrant with 20 bets and a great mean ranks below an entrant with 600 solid bets because their bound is wider. Ranking on the bound makes sample size a feature of the score, not a caveat under it.

rows.definition: A multiplicative haircut derived from the number of sealed entries and their pairwise overlap (Reality Check / SPA logic, implemented as a bootstrap max-T in engine/stats.py).
rows.why: Twenty entrants each trying thirty ideas is six hundred searches; the correction has to be applied to the whole field, or the leaderboard's winner is the entry that happened to look best.

rows.definition: Penalty proportional to the share of net PnL from the largest single season or single team cluster.
rows.why: Directly implements G-8: a strategy that is really about one year of one style is worth less than one that repeats, even at the same mean.

rows.definition: All EV figures net of the division's measured hold assumption (blocked at GAP-08; conservative floor until then).
rows.why: Without it, a parlay entry appears to beat a singles entry on a market where the house takes three times as much — a comparison of assumptions, not of skill.

rows.definition: Any failed hard gate sets the eligible score to zero regardless of magnitude.
rows.why: Rewards are the lever that makes the gates real. A gate that can be outweighed by a good month is a caption, not a control.

rows.definition: Every rank row shows n, EV_hat, LCB, t-statistic, abstain rate, CLV mean, and which gates failed.
rows.why: A leaderboard that hides its own inputs teaches nothing; the point of the competition is to learn which mechanisms generalise, which requires the losers' detail as much as the winners'.

sections.title: C. Rewards (non-cash by default)
sections.description: Rewards are chosen so the winning behaviour is the behaviour that grows the programme, and so that a cash prize does not arrive before a legal opinion does.

rows.reward: Capital promotion: the strategy moves from paper to a real stake allocation (capped at the owner's per-unit limit), plus first call on a licensed data request.
rows.condition: All hard gates passed; at least two seasons or one season plus one in-season walk-forward window; owner sign-off required (Q-01 is unanswered).
rows.why: The scarcest resource in this programme is not money, it is the right to place a bet and the licence to see a dataset. Paying in those selects for durability rather than for a hot month.

rows.reward: Compute and storage priority for the next development cycle; named authorship on the model card.
rows.condition: All hard gates except G-1 sample sufficiency (explicitly staged as 'pending sample').
rows.why: Keeps promising-but-undersized work alive without funding it, and makes credit the currency.

rows.reward: Fast-track review: a two-week path to sealed re-entry with the corrected specification.
rows.condition: Judged on the model card and the pre-registered hypothesis, never on the PnL of the trial.
rows.why: Counteracts the leaderboard's worst failure mode, which is that everyone farms last season's winner.

rows.reward: Graveyard entry with a permanent, prominent record plus the same compute priority as a 2nd place.
rows.condition: Reproducible kill: the failing evidence is committed with the data snapshot and the gate that tripped.
rows.why: We explicitly want the negative results, because they are the denominator that makes the multiple-comparison correction meaningful.

rows.reward: NOT OFFERED until legal review (Q-13, GAP-14).
rows.condition: counsel opinion, free entry, published rules, jurisdictional eligibility, tax handling.
rows.why: A paid-entry contest with a partly-luck ranking is the shape of a lottery; the league itself bars its personnel from daily fantasy and treats prediction markets as betting, which is a fair indication of how closely this neighbourhood is policed.

sections.title: D. Anti-gaming and integrity of the competition

rows.rule: Sealed entries: hash(code + config + data snapshot) submitted before the season starts; ranks computed only from the sealed version.
rows.defeats: Retro-fitting the strategy to what happened, and the quiet edit after a bad week.

rows.rule: Every decision is logged, including abstentions, with the modelled edge at the time.
rows.defeats: Survivorship inside a single entry: showing only the bets you would still take today.

rows.rule: Overlap test (Jaccard > 0.8 merges entries); max 5 live entries per author.
rows.defeats: Entering the same idea twenty times and keeping the winner — the winner's-curse reintroduced at the contest level (G-13).

rows.rule: Settlement only from the pre-declared official source; the operator's own settlement is used for void/reprice effects and nothing else.
rows.defeats: Stat-definition arbitrage and 'we would have won on a different definition' disputes (Q-03).

rows.rule: Price at bet time is captured from the posted line at that second, with the timestamp stored.
rows.defeats: Claiming a better price than was available, which fabricates CLV — the very statistic the ranking is built on.

rows.rule: No use of non-public information; inputs restricted to the source register by build-time check.
rows.defeats: The one 'edge' that would end the programme and possibly more: leaked availability information (Q-23, GAP-11).

rows.rule: Stake caps are part of the rules, not advice: an entry that exceeds the exposure caps is disqualified, not penalised.
rows.defeats: Winning by taking a ruinous amount of risk on a positive-variance bet.

rows.rule: Independent validator: a second person (or session) re-runs the winning entry from the sealed artefacts before a reward is paid.
rows.defeats: Everything the builder of a model cannot see about their own model (S-19).

rows.gate_set: pre-registered hypothesis and falsifying test written down (models.json B)
G-9 walk-forward discipline on the split, G-4 selectivity, G-12 compliance
G-1 sample, G-2 hurdle, G-3 CLV, G-5 multiple comparisons, G-6 deflator
all hard gates plus G-7 measured hold, G-10 costs and limits, G-8 concentration
re-verified each season by an independent validator; annual re-approval
rows.exit: two consecutive failing reviews = retirement, no appeal
